surfaces.part: middle shelf board with helmets above it

answer.evidence: Rows 1-4 form a top band of lighter wood that ends in a bright front-edge line at row 4. Dark interior starts directly below at row 5. The open compartments show helmets inside (rows 5-12 and 18-24), and shelf boards at rows 13 and 25 show a light top edge over a front strip. The front face, with open compartments and shelf fronts, runs about rows 5-31. No receding side face is drawn. The top band is 4 rows, so it is more than a rim, and the visible contents add more depth evidence.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden shelf with helmets on two tiers. It has 23 distinct colours and a median of 15 per tile, close to the stall (17) and well (20) and above the hedge (10). Flat-fill coverage is 15%, about the same as the stall's 13%. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans brown and follows the wood, which matches dark_material_tone. The wood has about 4 lightness steps (highlight, light, mid, dark) and shows some grain. The helmets have small highlights and shading, but they are small and fairly simple. The back panel and the shelf boards look somewhat flat compared with the roof tiles and stonework on the stall and well, which carry 5-6 steps and per-element texture. Its colour count is well below the stall (40) and well (38). A careful artist would probably find it a little thinner than the best references, though it does not look like a sticker. It is borderline and slightly lower, so I fail it on the 'when in doubt, fail' rule.

surfaces.part: top board of the shelf unit

The silhouette is a constant 32 px wide, so no side face is drawn. The top band is shallow but has a visible edge line, which is similar to the green cabinet reference.
